tools.name: search_hotels
tools.title: Search hotels in a city (Tutu.ru)
tools.description: Search Tutu hotel listings for a given city and date range. Resolve `city_name` (string) OR pass `geo_id` (Tutu internal). Returns hotels with `name`, `stars`, `rating`, `address`, `hotel_id` / `hotel_geo_id` (numeric id for get_offer_details), `tutu_offer_id` (listing UUID, not accepted by details), `review_summary` (when Tutu has reviews), `location`, `photos`, `best_offer` (`price` + `offerpack_hash` + `checkout_url` + `room_size_sqm` (room area in m² when Tutu wrote it in the room name, often as a minimum 'от N'; `null` when absent — say so, don't infer) + normalized rate features: `breakfast_included`, `meal_name`, `free_cancellation`, `pay_at_hotel`, `pay_online`, plus raw `highlights[]` for promo/context badges) — here `checkout_url` IS a real per-hotel page (`hotel.tutu.ru/offers/details?...`) with dates and room composition pre-filled, unlike the transport tools. For checkout PREFER `create_checkout_link` with the row's `checkout_ref` — the `explicit/hotel` deeplink opens the hotel page to pick a room, or mints the cart straight-to-cart when you pass a ROOM rate's `offerpack_hash` from `get_offer_details` (the listing `best_offer.offerpack_hash` does NOT mint a cart); `best_offer.checkout_url` stays the direct-page fallback when the tool's link isn't available. Filters: `stars`, `meals`, `hotel_types`, `min_rating`, `price_max`, `free_cancellation`, `breakfast_included`, `hotel_amenities` (e.g. `pool`, `parking`, `wifi`, `spa`), `room_amenities` (e.g. `sea_view`, `balcony`, `air_conditioner`). Paginated (`page`+`page_size`, see `meta.has_more`). Read-only, no booking. When the request is broad, many hotels are viable, and you don't know the user's preferences — do NOT call this tool yet: ask one short batch of clarifying questions FIRST (bed setup, breakfast, free-cancel, view/location; 2-4 questions max). But that gate is OFF whenever the user hands you the decision — a deterministic selection rule ('первый найденный', 'самый дешёвый', 'выбери сам', 'лишь бы переночевать', 'без уточняющих вопросов') or an explicit checkout intent ('оформляй', 'кинь ссылку'). Then the preferences you weren't told are the ones that don't matter: search now, apply their rule to the results and hand over the link in the SAME turn. The only thing still worth asking for is a REQUIRED field you cannot fill — the city and the dates, which this tool rejects the call without; never invent those. A preference is never that field. Judge that intent, don't pattern-match those examples as a closed list. Generic positive framing ('хорошее место', 'бюджет не критичен') is NOT a selection rule — still ask. When the per-room / per-rate confirmation field for the asked-for feature is missing or mismatched — `rooms[i].view` / `rooms[i].bed_type` for view/bed, or `rooms[i].rates[j].breakfast_included` / `rooms[i].rates[j].free_cancellation` for the rate-level facets, or `best_offer.{breakfast_included,free_cancellation}` when only listing data is available — label the status next to the recommendation; never substitute silently. Full rules in `get_hotels_instructions` (clarifying questions, geo_id pitfall, view/bed grounding). Grounding: rating, review count, amenities and pros/cons must come from `review_summary`, `review_summary.aspects` and from `get_offer_details(product_type='hotel', ...)`. The `best_offer` fields describe ONLY the cheapest visible rate of one room — to compare room categories (standard / comfort / suite, beds, view, size) and full per-rate options, call `get_offer_details`. Never invent guest quotes or substitute generic city-level praise when the hotel-level field is empty. `best_offer.price` is the TOTAL for the whole requested stay and guest composition (`price_basis="stay_total"`, the night count already included) — render it as-is and NEVER multiply it by the number of nights; `stay.nights` is there only to label it 'за N ночей'. See `get_hotels_instructions`.

check_in.description: Check-in date, YYYY-MM-DD. `checkin_date` is accepted as a backward-compatible alias.
check_in.title: Check In

check_out.description: Check-out date, YYYY-MM-DD. `checkout_date` is accepted as a backward-compatible alias. Must be after check_in.
check_out.title: Check Out

city_name.description: City name (Russian; English/translit also accepted). Resolved via Tutu's hotel-specific, region-aware geo index: a resort name lands the whole zone (e.g. «Курорт Архыз» covering several посёлки), a city lands that city. `meta.resolved_geo` reports `geo_type` (region|locality), `hotels_count` and `also_geo` alternatives. PREFER this over passing `geo_id` directly. Mutually-optional with `geo_id`.
city_name.title: City Name

geo_id.description: Tutu hotel city geo_id (e.g. '2657260' for Moscow, '2656873' for Казань). Skip the city_name lookup if provided. WARNING: only pass an id obtained from a previous `search_hotels` response (`meta.geo_id` or `meta.resolved_geo.geo_id`). Do NOT reuse geo_ids from transport tools (`search_avia` / `search_rail` / `search_bus` / `search_etrain`) — for some cities those resolve to an AIRPORT/STATION entry that has zero hotels in Tutu's hotel catalog.
geo_id.title: Geo Id

children_ages.description: Ages of accompanying children, e.g. [6, 12]. Empty/None = no children.
children_ages.title: Children Ages

stars.description: Filter: include only these star ratings (1..5, plus 0 for unrated). Multi-select.
stars.title: Stars

price_max.description: Filter: maximum price PER NIGHT (RUB). Sent to the upstream as a relevance signal, then enforced server-side as a hard cap on `best_offer.price.amount / stay.nights` — the offer price is a whole-stay total, so it's divided back to per-night before the comparison.
price_max.title: Price Max

min_rating.description: Filter: minimum aggregated rating (0..10). Mapped to the nearest Tutu rating bucket (>0 / >7 / >8 / >9).
min_rating.title: Min Rating

free_cancellation.description: Filter: keep only offers whose cheapest rate advertises free cancellation. Sent via `popular_filters`; treat as best-effort upstream — verify with `best_offer.free_cancellation` per row.
free_cancellation.title: Free Cancellation

breakfast_included.description: Filter: keep only offers whose cheapest rate includes breakfast. Shortcut for `meals=['breakfast']` plus the `popular_filters` quick toggle.
breakfast_included.title: Breakfast Included

hotel_amenities.description: Filter: property-level amenities. Aliases: `pool`, `parking`, `wifi`, `spa`, `transfer`, `kid_friendly`, `pet_friendly`, `kitchen`, `fitness`, `sauna`, `jacuzzi`, `aquapark`, `kids_pool`, `beach`, `elevator`, `minibar`, `fridge`, `buffet`. Raw Tutu amenity ids (e.g. `'2005'`) are also accepted.
hotel_amenities.title: Hotel Amenities

room_amenities.description: Filter: room-level amenities (best-effort at the listing upstream — the response carries one `best_offer`, so use `get_offer_details` for guaranteed per-room filtering). Aliases: `sea_view`, `mountain_view`, `view`, `balcony`, `air_conditioner`, `private_bath`, `room_wifi`, `room_kitchen`, `workspace`. Raw Tutu amenity ids (e.g. `'2014'`) are also accepted.
room_amenities.title: Room Amenities

view.description: Response detail level: `compact` (default) or `full`. `compact` keeps one cover photo per hotel; `full` keeps a small gallery (a handful of photos, not every one — `photos_total` records the real count, the rest live on the hotel page). Room categories, rate ladders and review texts come from `get_offer_details` regardless of `view`. Prefer `compact` for first-pass search — `full` only swaps in more photos, which an agent rarely needs and which can overflow client output caps.
view.title: View

tools.name: search_avia
tools.title: Search air tickets (Tutu.ru)
tools.description: Search Tutu air tickets between two cities or specific airports. PRICE BASIS — every `price` already covers the WHOLE searched party (`adults` + `children` + `infants`; `meta.pricing.basis="party_total"`, verified live). Never multiply it by the passenger count. NB the sibling tools differ: `search_rail` / `search_etrain` quote ONE SEAT. `origin`/`destination` accept a city ('Москва'), an airport name ('Шереметьево') or a bare IATA code ('SVO', 'IST'). An airport input narrows the city-wide search to that airport: offers via the city's other airports are dropped (count in `meta.post_filter_dropped_wrong_airport`; the key is present only when the request named a specific airport), the endpoint gets `meta.from/to.kind="airport"` and its `iata` becomes the airport's own code. A bare code means the airport, not the metro area ('IST' = Стамбул-Новый only, SAW dropped); pass the city name to cover all its airports. When every city flight uses other airports, `meta.airport_note` lists them with counts — relay it and offer a city-wide retry. `meta.from/to` echo the resolved place (`name`, `geo_id`, `region`); `match` + `query` are added only when the resolved name differs from the wording sent (`lead` = a short form or typo read by Tutu's own ranking — say which city came back and keep going; `qualified` = the trailing words acted as a region filter; `prefix`), and `also_named[]` lists same-name places that lost — mention them, never as a blocking question. An ambiguous or unknown name is REFUSED with `could not resolve …` (the equal candidates with regions, or a note that only Tutu's hotel index lists the place — then offer `search_hotels`), never searched as another city: ask the user or resend as '<name>, <область>' (name first). A place without an airport is refused too; the text names the city Tutu's avia index answers with (Сочи for Хоста) — OFFER that city and search it only after the user agrees, never pick an airport city on your own. Supports one-way and round-trip (`return_date`). Each offer carries: `price` (cheapest fare), `variants[]` (every fare family with its own `offer_hash` for checkout), `legs[].segments[]` (full itinerary with `voyage_no` flight numbers, including `review_summary` for the carrier when Tutu returns feedback), `search_results_url` (tutu.ru listing page — not a per-offer URL), and `checkout_ref` (pass verbatim to `create_checkout_link` to get a deeplink purchase URL for the exact ticket plus a search-results URL for browsing — show the deeplink when the user has chosen this specific flight. A Direct ROUND-TRIP offers are deeplinkable too: `checkout_ref` carries `is_round_trip` + `return_departure_at` — forward BOTH and the deeplink mints a cart with both legs. Connecting round-trips fall back to search because explicit/avia currently supports one flight per direction; omitting `return_departure_at` also falls back to search. `checkout_ref` also carries `passengers_full/child/infant` from the search so the cart can request the same party — forward them, else the cart opens with one adult. An offer flagged `is_multi_pnr` (one-way OR round-trip) means separate tickets / self-transfer — relay its `multi_pnr_note`; on a ONE-WAY such an offer also gets `checkout_ref.checkout_parts`, which must be forwarded because `create_checkout_link` cannot put such a trip in one link — it answers with one link per ticket). For a presentation card, pass the selected compact offer object as `details_ref` to `get_offer_details(product_type='avia', ...)`; there is no separate read-only avia detail endpoint. Paginated (`page`+`page_size`, see `meta.has_more`) — a page is a WINDOW over the matched flights, NOT the day's timetable: a flight absent from the current page may still operate, so never answer «такого рейса нет» from one page while `has_more` is true; when the user names a flight, pass `flight_numbers` instead of paging blind — and an empty NUMBER-ONLY result means «нет в продаже на Tutu на эту дату» (the flight may still operate), never a timetable claim — and only while `meta.total_matched_exact` is true: on a rare capped route (`false`) the filter saw a truncated pool, so the check is INCONCLUSIVE — say that instead of «нет». With other filters also active (`price_max` / `carriers` / `direct_only` / airport scope) even that much doesn't follow — the flight may be dropped by one of those (see `meta.post_filter_dropped_*`); re-run number-only before concluding. Sortable by price / duration / departure time. Filterable server-side: `direct_only` (nonstop only), `carriers` (by airline) and `flight_numbers` (by flight designator). `meta.carriers_available` is the per-route airline reference (`name` + `offers_count` + `price_from`, derived from the fetched route pool; a stable `id` is added only when Tutu ships its carrier facet) — filter by echoing a `name` from it rather than guessing spelling. Filter drop counts surface in `meta.post_filter_dropped_not_direct` / `..._dropped_wrong_carrier` / `..._dropped_wrong_flight_number`. With a filter active the whole route pool is fetched before filtering, so a carrier listed in `carriers_available` reliably appears and `has_more` stays honest; `meta.total_matched` is the exact count after filters, before pagination (`meta.total_matched_exact=false` only on a rare >200-offer route, where it is a lower bound). Grounding: every claim about baggage, cabin baggage, refund, change, seat selection, fare family or carrier rating must be traceable to `variants[].conditions` or `review_summary` in this response. If a field is null/absent, say so explicitly — never fall back to general knowledge of the carrier or to web search. Airport disambiguation is mandatory: each `legs[].segments[].to` is a self-describing string `"City — Name (IATA), терм. T"` (e.g. `"Стамбул — Сабиха Гёкчен (SAW)"`) — surface the airport name and terminal verbatim, and call out when two offers in the same list use different airports of the same city (SAW vs IST for Стамбул, SVO / DME / VKO / ZIA for Москва). Say that they are different airports, but do not add distance, side-of-city or transfer facts absent from the payload. When the upstream omitted the name the string falls back to `"City, IATA"`; then IATA → airport-name is acceptable common knowledge (stable global registry). `meta.cashback` is normally ABSENT here — flights earn none today — so say nothing about cashback unless the key is present. When it is, it states the whole page's Tutu loyalty rate (`rate_pct`; `applies_to` = `all_fares` / `most_fares` / `some_fares` with `rows_at_rate` of `rows_total` fare rows; `exceptions[]` for the rows that differ): bonus points credited to the buyer's Tutu account after payment, NOT money off `price`, never to be presented as a discount. For airport disambiguation and checkout details call `get_avia_instructions`.

origin.description: Origin city (e.g. 'Москва', 'Moscow', 'Сочи') or a specific airport by name/IATA code ('Внуково', 'VKO') — an airport narrows results to it. Resolved via Tutu suggest: short forms («Питер», «Мск») resolve server-side — `meta.from` then carries `match` + `query`, plus `also_named` when a same-name place lost. If the tool refuses with candidates (`could not resolve …`), ask the user or resend as '<name>, <область>' (name first). `from_city` is accepted as a backward-compatible alias.
origin.title: Origin

destination.description: Destination city or a specific airport by name/IATA code ('Шереметьево', 'SVO') — an airport narrows results to it. Resolved via Tutu suggest: short forms («Питер», «Мск») resolve server-side — `meta.to` then carries `match` + `query`, plus `also_named` when a same-name place lost. If the tool refuses with candidates (`could not resolve …`), ask the user or resend as '<name>, <область>' (name first). `to_city` is accepted as a backward-compatible alias.
destination.title: Destination

return_date.description: Optional return date, YYYY-MM-DD. When set, the tool asks upstream for a round-trip package and returns offers with both legs (`legs[0]=outbound`, `legs[1]=return`). Crucial for long-haul international routes — some city pairs (e.g. Tokyo→Moscow far-future) are sold only as round-trip and return 0 offers as one-way.
return_date.title: Return Date

service_class.description: IATA service class: Y=economy, S=premium economy, C=business, F=first.
service_class.title: Service Class

page.description: 1-indexed page number. Each page carries up to `page_size` offers. Check `meta.has_more` to know if another page exists.
page.title: Page

sort.description: Ordering applied before pagination. `price_asc` (cheapest first), `price_desc`, `duration_asc` (shortest first), `departure_asc` (earliest departure).
sort.title: Sort

price_max.description: Hard cap on price per offer (RUB). Enforced server-side.
price_max.title: Price Max

direct_only.description: Keep only nonstop flights (every leg a single segment; correct for round-trip). Client-side post-filter; dropped count in `meta.post_filter_dropped_not_direct`.
direct_only.title: Direct Only

carriers.description: Keep only offers by these airlines. Pass a `name` from `meta.carriers_available` (e.g. 'Аэрофлот'); an `id` also works when that entry carries one. Do NOT guess spelling: 'aeroflot' will not match 'Аэрофлот'. Case-insensitive substring on the display name; all carriers on a multi-carrier offer must match one of the requested values. An empty list is a no-op. Dropped count in `meta.post_filter_dropped_wrong_carrier`.
carriers.title: Carriers

flight_numbers.description: Keep only offers containing one of these flights — THE way to answer «возьми рейс N»: one call instead of paging through the day. Accepts the full designator in any spelling ('SU-6176', 'SU 6176', 'su6176' — case, separators and leading zeros are normalized) or the bare flight digits ('6176', matched against every segment's number). ANY-segment match: a connection or round-trip containing the named flight keeps the WHOLE itinerary. Applied client-side to the full route pool (upstream has no flight-number filter); an empty list is a no-op. Dropped count in `meta.post_filter_dropped_wrong_flight_number`. An empty NUMBER-ONLY result means «этого рейса нет в продаже на Tutu на эту дату» — the flight may still operate (sold out or not sold here); never turn it into a timetable claim. That reading itself holds only while `meta.total_matched_exact` is true — on a rare capped route (`false`) the filter saw a truncated pool and the check is inconclusive. Combined with other filters it proves even less — the flight may be dropped by price/carrier/direct/airport scope (see their `meta.post_filter_dropped_*` counters); re-run number-only before concluding.
flight_numbers.title: Flight Numbers

view.description: Response detail level: `compact` (default) or `full`. `compact` returns lean decision cards — rail collapses the long per-class fare list to a `fares` summary {count, price_from, price_to, currency, refundable_count?, changeable_count?, refundable_unknown?, changeable_unknown?} (the full per-class breakdown and car classes come from `get_offer_details`; per-variant `conditions: {refundable, changeable}` come with `view='full'`), and rail/bus drop the per-segment rating that duplicates the offer-level one. Avia and etrain are left unchanged — neither has a read-only detail endpoint to recover dropped fares/ratings from. `full` inlines every fare variant and per-segment review_summary. Prefer `compact` for first-pass search; pass `full` only when the user needs the whole fare breakdown inline for several offers at once.
view.title: View

tools.name: search_rail
tools.title: Search railway tickets (Tutu.ru)
tools.description: Search Russian Railways (РЖД) tickets between two cities. Returns the real departure & arrival station names per offer (useful when a city has several stations — Москва has Курский / Ленинградский / Казанский). `origin`/`destination` take a city or a station name (a station resolves when Tutu's index returns the station row, e.g. «Ярославский вокзал»; otherwise city-level). `meta.from/to` echo the resolved place (`name`, `geo_id`, `region`); `match` + `query` are added only when the resolved name differs from the wording sent (`lead` = a short form or typo read by Tutu's own ranking — say which city came back and keep going; `qualified` = the trailing words acted as a region filter; `prefix`), and `also_named[]` lists same-name places that lost — mention them, never as a blocking question. An ambiguous or unknown name is REFUSED with `could not resolve …` (the equal candidates with regions, or a note that only Tutu's hotel index lists the place — then offer `search_hotels`), never searched as another city: ask the user or resend as '<name>, <область>' (name first). PRICE BASIS — every amount here is ONE SEAT: `price`, `fares.price_from` / `price_to`, `seat_categories[].price_from` and a transfer plan's `price_from` are one ticket, because upstream prices a train fare per passenger and never scales it by the party (unlike `search_avia` / `search_bus`, whose prices already cover everyone). `meta.pricing.basis="per_seat"` states this on every page; with `passengers` > 1 each offer additionally carries `price_party` (that offer's cheapest fare x passengers) and a transfer plan `price_party_from`. Quote `price_party` as «от» — it assumes the whole party travels on ONE fare row, which holds only while that row still seats them (`seats_left >= N`, `view='full'`); a mixed-class party pays more. Never present a bare `price` as the total for several travellers. Each offer carries: `price`, a `fares` summary in the default `compact` view (`{count, price_from, price_to, currency, refundable_count?, changeable_count?, refundable_unknown?, changeable_unknown?, seat_categories?, uncategorized_fares?}` — the counts say how many fare rows are KNOWN refundable / exchangeable, so `refundable_count: 0` means «none confirmed refundable», not «no refundable fare exists»; `refundable_unknown` / `changeable_unknown` count the rows upstream left unresolved on that field (absent when every row resolved it), and while they are present the zero proves nothing — say the check was inconclusive for N тарифов instead of denying. A count itself is absent when NO row resolved the field; `seat_categories` maps each car category present on the train to `{count, price_from}` — `SEDENTARY` (сидячий) / `RESERVED_SEAT` (плацкарт) / `COMPARTMENT` (купе) / `LUX` (СВ) / `SOFT` / `SHARED` (общий) — so «есть ли сидячка и почём» is answered here, without `get_offer_details` / `get_rail_seatmap`. A missing category means it is NOT on sale — unless `uncategorized_fares` is present, which counts fare rows upstream left unclassified, so absence proves nothing until they're resolved. It bounds the refund / exchange counts as well ONLY when you passed `seat_categories`: that filter deletes those rows before the summary is built, so re-run WITHOUT the filter — `view='full'` cannot bring them back. Unfiltered, they stay counted. Never add `uncategorized_fares` to the `*_unknown` counters; the per-class ladder купе / плацкарт / СВ with names + amenities comes from `get_offer_details` and nowhere else. `view='full'` inlines the full `variants[]` instead — no class cards, but each row carries `conditions: {refundable, changeable}` so you can tell WHICH price is the refundable one, plus `seat_category`, `service_class` (Express-3 code like 2С / 3Э), the same `uncategorized_fares` count at OFFER level (there is no `fares` block in that view) and `seats_left` (seats on sale for that fare row — a party of N needs `seats_left >= N`; do NOT sum it across rows, tariffs of one class share inventory)), `legs[].segments[]` with carrier + train number + train brand (`vehicle_meta`: `name` like «Ласточка» / «Сапсан» when branded, plus `is_premium` / `is_double_decker` when true — an unbranded двухэтажный still carries the flag with no `name`; omitted only for a plain train) + `review_summary` when Tutu has train feedback, `search_results_url` (tutu.ru listing page), and `checkout_ref` — the handoff object for `create_checkout_link` (offers deliberately carry NO ready checkout link: the link comes from that tool). `details_ref` can be passed to `get_offer_details(product_type='rail', ...)` to load `service_classes[]` (one card per class: description, structured `amenities[]` codes like WIFI / AIR_CONDITIONING / BIO_TOILET with Russian labels, rating, photos), lean fare rows in `variants[]` (join to the class card via `class_index`), `cars[]`, and a `train_vehicle` block (name, is_premium, is_firm, is_double_decker, has_photo, has_tour_3d) plus a `ticket` block. For amenity-code localization see `tutu://amenities/dictionary`. Car CATEGORY (сидячий / плацкарт / купе / СВ) is answered here; this search alone does NOT answer female/male/mixed compartment, exact-seat, nearby-seat, lower/upper or WC-distance questions — for those, the next step is `get_rail_seatmap(details_ref=offer.details_ref)` on the chosen offer (use its `task=` modes for gender/far-from-WC). Paginated + sortable — and a page is a WINDOW over the matched trains (default 10 per page, cheapest-first), NOT the day's schedule: `meta.total_matched` is how many trains matched in total, `meta.has_more` says pages remain. A train absent from the current page may still run that day, so NEVER answer «такого поезда нет» from one page while `has_more` is true — when the user names a specific train, pass `train_numbers` instead of paging blind. And mind what an empty filtered result proves: in a NUMBER-ONLY search it means «билетов на этот поезд в продаже нет» — and no more: the pool lists BOOKABLE trains only (sold-out and notify-only trains are excluded upstream), so the train may still run. Say «нет в продаже на эту дату», never a timetable claim («не ходит/не существует»). With OTHER filters also active (`price_max` / `seat_categories` / `carriers` / `direct_only`) even that much doesn't follow — the named train may be dropped by one of THOSE (each names its removals in `meta.post_filter_dropped_*`), so re-run number-only before concluding. And even number-only, the conclusion covers DIRECT trains: on a route answered by transfer plans the `meta.interchange_routes` block is nondeterministic upstream (the same request may return no plans on a given call), so an absent or emptied transfer block proves nothing — say «прямых поездов с этим номером в продаже нет» and treat the transfer side as unverified. When NO train runs the whole route on that date, `offers` is empty and `meta.interchange_routes` carries transfer plans instead — two or more legs, and a leg is a train, a coach or a flight (cheapest first; `meta.interchange_routes_total` is how many exist). Every filter binds this block too and says what it removed: `direct_only=true` suppresses it entirely; `price_max` caps plans by their TRIP total (`meta.interchange_routes_dropped_over_cap`); `carriers` → `..._dropped_wrong_carrier`; `train_numbers` keeps plans with the named train on ANY leg (`..._dropped_wrong_train_number`); `seat_categories` requires the category on every TRAIN leg and re-prices the plan from those fares (a coach or flight leg has no car categories, so it is not judged and keeps its own price; an all-non-train plan cannot satisfy the request and is dropped) (`..._dropped_wrong_seat_category`, plus `..._unverified_seat_category` when a leg still holds unclassified fares). An empty block with a non-zero DROPPED count is «есть, но не проходят фильтр»; with a non-zero UNVERIFIED count it is «не удалось проверить категорию» — neither is «вариантов нет». Check this before saying «поездов нет». A plan is a ROUTE SUGGESTION, not an offer: no `checkout_ref` / `details_ref` / seat map / single link for the whole trip (all of those describe ONE ride, and Tutu itself sells a transfer as separate orders, one per leg). Read `legs[].type` FIRST — a plan may mix `train`, `bus` and `avia` legs, and the rest of the leg reads off it; say which is which when presenting. So with `adults` > 1 every variant also carries `price_party` — the comparable total for the searched party — and that is what the `price` ranking, `meta.modes_summary.<mode>.min_price_party` and any cross-mode comparison must use; `min_price` and `price` stay each product's own number. `meta.pricing` says which basis is in force. Comparing raw `price` across modes at `adults` > 1 makes the train look ~N times cheaper than it is. The rail `price_party` is «от»: it assumes the party fits one fare row. NB rail can also answer OUTSIDE that list: on a route with no direct train, `meta.modes_summary.railway.interchange_routes` holds transfer PLANS (legs may be train, coach or flight) while `variants[]` stays empty for that mode — they are route suggestions, not bookable variants (no single ticket, cart or link for the whole trip), so they are not ranked among the others. Do NOT read an empty rail entry as «поездов нет» without checking that block; the same filter counters ride along (`interchange_routes_dropped_over_cap` / `..._wrong_carrier` / `..._wrong_seat_category` / `..._unverified_seat_category`), and a non-zero one next to an empty block means «есть, но не проходят фильтр», not «нет». Shape and booking rules are identical to `search_rail`'s `meta.interchange_routes` — see `get_rail_instructions`. `meta.modes_summary.<mode>.searched` appears when that mode resolved a side to a DIFFERENT place than `meta.from` / `meta.to` — it happens when the wording names an airport, whose row and its city's row carry different geo_ids. Say it out loud when present: those offers depart from the place named there, not from the page's. `meta.modes_summary.<mode>.cashback` carries that mode's Tutu loyalty rate (per mode — the rate differs by product): bonus points credited to the buyer's Tutu account after payment, NOT money off `price`, never to be presented as a discount. Absent for a mode that earns none. It is tagged `scope: "mode_page"`: the rate and the `rows_at_rate` / `rows_total` counters describe that mode's own FETCHED page (same population as the `count` / `min_price` beside them) — neither the merged page nor everything the mode matched, so never call that coverage exhaustive. `exceptions[]` is narrowed to offers on the merged page, and the full per-fare breakdown comes from that mode's own `search_*`. What this count does per mode: avia and bus are PRICED for it upstream, while rail and etrain are not (a train fare is one seat whatever the party), so above 1 it is what `price_party` / `min_price_party` are computed with and what the `price` ranking uses.
adults.title: Adults

modes.description: Subset of modes to include. Default: all four.
modes.title: Modes

optimize_for.description: Sort variants by total price (default) or by total trip duration.
optimize_for.title: Optimize For

page_size.description: Variants per page after merging across modes.
page_size.title: Page Size

price_max.description: Hard cap on price per variant (RUB), read as a budget for the whole searched party. Applied to every mode independently and always in the party basis: avia and bus test it against their own (already whole-party) price, while rail and etrain — which quote one seat — test `price_max / adults`, so one cap means the same money everywhere. Compare survivors on `price_party`.
price_max.title: Price Max

direct_only.description: Keep only direct offers (no transfers) in every mode. Applied per-mode, like `price_max`.
direct_only.title: Direct Only

carriers.description: Keep only offers by these carriers in every mode. Case-insensitive substring on carrier display names (pass values echoed from a per-mode search's `meta.carriers_available`); an empty list is a no-op. All carriers on a multi-carrier offer must match one of the requested values. Applied per-mode, like `price_max`.
carriers.title: Carriers

view.description: Response detail level: `compact` (default) or `full`. `compact` returns lean decision cards — rail collapses the long per-class fare list to a `fares` summary {count, price_from, price_to, currency, refundable_count?, changeable_count?, refundable_unknown?, changeable_unknown?} (the full per-class breakdown and car classes come from `get_offer_details`; per-variant `conditions: {refundable, changeable}` come with `view='full'`), and rail/bus drop the per-segment rating that duplicates the offer-level one. Avia and etrain are left unchanged — neither has a read-only detail endpoint to recover dropped fares/ratings from. `full` inlines every fare variant and per-segment review_summary. Prefer `compact` for first-pass search; pass `full` only when the user needs the whole fare breakdown inline for several offers at once.
view.title: View

tools.name: get_offer_details
tools.title: Get offer details (Tutu.ru)
tools.description: Fetch details for a single offer. Defaults to `view='compact'`: for hotels it caps photos, omits the per-rate `cancellation_policy` text (the `free_cancellation` / `free_cancellation_until` flags stay), omits room `amenity_groups` (flat `room_amenities` stays) and omits review TEXTS — the `review_summary` aggregate stays. Use `view='rules'` for the exact cancellation ladder, `view='reviews'` + `review_limit` for a feedback-only card (review texts with pagination; rooms collapse to stubs), or `view='full'` for everything. Transport details ignore `view`. `product_type=hotels` takes the hotel id under any of `offer_id` / `hotel_id` / `hotel_geo_id` — three names for the SAME value, so copy the field off the `search_hotels` row and pass exactly one (two different ids is an error: it means two rows got mixed). It returns hotel info (name, address, photos, hotel-level amenities, rules, `review_summary`) plus `rooms[]` — every room category Tutu sells, each with: `room_name`, `room_description`, `photos`, `bed_summary` + `bed_type` (single/twin/double), `view` (sea/water/mountain/park/city/river/lake/yard/other when Tutu wrote it into the room name), `room_size_sqm` (room area in m² when Tutu exposes it, often a minimum 'от N'; usually `null` here — the detail upstream rarely carries area, the listing `best_offer.room_size_sqm` is the more reliable source — so say 'площадь не указана', don't guess) and `max_occupancy` (None when Tutu doesn't provide it), `amenity_groups` grouped by Спальня/Ванная/Техника, flat `room_amenities`, structured `room_property_items`, `price_from` (THIS room's cheapest rate, same `{amount, currency, price_basis}` shape as a rate price — quote a room's price from here so name, size, view and price all come off ONE object; `null` when no rate is priced), and `rates[]`. Each rate carries `price` (the WHOLE-STAY total for the requested dates and guests, tagged `price_basis="stay_total"` — render as-is, NEVER multiply by nights; the top-level `stay {check_in, check_out, nights}` block carries the night count), `meal {included, name, type}`, `breakfast_included`, `refundable`, `free_cancellation` + `free_cancellation_until`, full `cancellation_policy[]`, `pay_at_hotel`, `pay_online`, raw `highlights[]`, and `offerpack_hash`. When `rooms` is empty AND `notices[]` carries `kind=no_room_offers_for_dates`, this is Tutu's encoding of 'provider has no inventory on these dates' (often transient — same hotel+dates can return rooms within the hour). Surface `notices[].agent_hint` to the user as the explanation, do not treat it as a tool error; the hotel's static info (name, address, photos, amenities, rating, reviews) is still populated. `product_type=rail` uses `offer.details_ref` from search_rail to load `service_classes[]` — one card per class (купе/плацкарт/СВ code in `service_class`, `description`, `services`, `amenities[]` with codes + Russian labels, per-class `review_summary`, `photos`) — plus lean fare rows in `variants[]` ({offer_hash, price, fare_type REFUNDABLE/NON_REFUNDABLE, service_class, class_index, car_type, car_number, seat_type, seats_count}; `class_index` points into `service_classes[]` — join by it, not by the display name), `cars[]` (per-car availability — sum `cars[].seats_count` for the train's free-seat total; do NOT sum `variants[].seats_count`, fare rows share seat groups so summing them double-counts), `train_vehicle` (name, is_premium / is_firm / is_double_decker, has_photo, has_tour_3d) and a `ticket` block (format=eticket, boarding=by_passport). `product_type=bus` uses `offer.details_ref` from search_bus to load structured `amenities[]` (Wi-Fi / power_outlet / air_conditioning / toilet flags), `bus_category` (model + service class), `ticket` (eticket flag + documents_accepted), `refund.blocks[]` and `luggage.blocks[]` with structured rule text, plus `seat_selection` (required, free_count, available_seat_ids, has_scheme). For bus straight-to-cart, pick `seat_numbers` only from `available_seat_ids`; if that list is empty or missing but `free_count` is positive, say that exact-seat preselection is unavailable in this response, NOT that there are no seats. `product_type=etrain` returns the search-envelope fallback with `summary.vehicle_type` (Ласточка vs Дальний with description) and a `ticket` block. `product_type=avia` can format a selected search offer passed as `details_ref`; the richer avia order endpoint is not called here because it creates a draft order. For amenity-code localization see `tutu://amenities/dictionary`.

product_type.description: Type of offer to inspect. Only `hotels` has text reviews; rail/bus have read-only detail endpoints.
product_type.title: Product Type

offer_id.description: REQUIRED for `hotels` (or its aliases `hotel_id` / `hotel_geo_id` — same value, pass any ONE): Tutu hotel id, i.e. the `hotel_id` / `hotel_geo_id` field of the search_hotels row you are detailing, the numeric id used in details URLs; `tutu_offer_id` UUID is not accepted by Tutu details endpoints. Optional for transport — `details_ref` alone is enough.
offer_id.title: Offer Id

hotel_id.description: Alias for `offer_id`, named as `search_hotels` returns it. Pass one of the three, not several.
hotel_id.title: Hotel Id

hotel_geo_id.description: Alias for `offer_id`, named as `search_hotels` and `create_checkout_link` spell it.
hotel_geo_id.title: Hotel Geo Id

details_ref.description: For `rail` and `bus`: pass `offer.details_ref` from the corresponding search result verbatim. For `avia`/`etrain`: pass the selected compact offer object if you want a presentation-ready reformat without side effects.
details_ref.title: Details Ref

review_limit.description: For `hotels`: number of review texts to return in `view='reviews'` / `view='full'`. Default 5, max 50; page with `review_offset`. Ignored by `compact`/`rules` — those views carry only `review_summary` and skip the review fetch entirely.
review_limit.title: Review Limit

review_offset.description: For `hotels`: review pagination offset. Use `hotel.reviews.pagination.has_more` to fetch next page.
review_offset.title: Review Offset

review_sort.description: For `hotels`: sort review texts by date or rating.
review_sort.title: Review Sort

review_topics.description: For `hotels`: optional topic filter from `hotel.reviews.topics`. Empty/None = all topics.
review_topics.title: Review Topics

view.description: Response detail level. Hotel detail scope: `compact` (default) / `rules` / `reviews` / `full`. `compact` is the lean decision card: room photos capped, per-rate `cancellation_policy` text dropped (the decision facts stay in `free_cancellation` + `free_cancellation_until`), room `amenity_groups` dropped (flat `room_amenities` kept), hotel photos capped, hotel `amenity_groups` slimmed to names, and review TEXTS omitted — the `review_summary` aggregate (rating + aspects) stays; for guest quotes call `view='reviews'`. `rules` = compact + the full cancellation ladder. `reviews` is a feedback-only card: hotel identity + `review_summary` + `reviews[]` texts (set `review_limit`), rooms collapse to name + cheapest-price stubs, no photos/amenities/policy. `full` returns every block (photo arrays still bounded to a small gallery). Transport details ignore `view`.
view.title: View

tools.name: get_rail_seatmap
tools.title: Get rail seat map (Tutu.ru)
tools.description: Read-only per-car seat layout for a selected rail offer. Authoritative next step after `search_rail` for ANY question about exact seats, car layout, female/male/mixed compartments, lower/upper or nearby seats, or WC distance: if a rail offer has `details_ref`, CALL this — never tell the user the seat map is unavailable without calling, and read `seatmap_status` to tell a real layout (`ok`) from `no_layout_for_carrier`. Top-level `seatmap_status`: `"ok"` when Tutu returned a schema, `"no_layout_for_carrier"` when Tutu has none for that train. The fallback is RARE — every train sampled live returned a layout, commercial brands included — so treat a layout as the norm and never predict its absence. In the fallback case `cars=[]` and an `agent_hint` field spells out that this is NOT 'no seats' — just 'no schema'. On success, `cars[]` carries every car of the train: `{car_number, car_type, service_class, amenities[], seat_groups[], seats[], hints, canvas}`. Each seat has `number`, `type`, `compartment_number`, `deck` (`None` unless double-decker), `gender`, `position{x,y}`, `size{width,height}`, plus precomputed `distance_to_nearest_wc_px` (Euclidean, server-side) so the agent quotes a ready number instead of doing geometry. The default `view='compact'` omits the raw geometry (`position`, `size`, `nearest_wc_rect`); pass `view='full'` to draw the car. For a pointed question prefer `task=` over paging the whole map: `far_from_wc` / `female` / `together` / `summary` return a short ranked answer across the WHOLE train (best seats + why), not every seat. `task='together'` (+ `seats_together`, default 2) answers «N мест рядом» directly — do NOT page the map and reason about coordinates or compartment numbers yourself. Seat `type` is an OPEN vocabulary: LOWER / UPPER / SIDE_LOWER / SIDE_UPPER / SEDENTARY are the common values, but variants occur live (`LOWER_NEAR_WC`, `UPPER_NEAR_WC`, `SEDENTARY_WITH_PETS`). Match by PREFIX, not equality: a lower berth is any type starting `LOWER` OR `SIDE_LOWER` (`SIDE_LOWER` does NOT start with `LOWER`), and `SIDE_*` is the separate side-of-car test. `type == "LOWER"` silently drops both `LOWER_NEAR_WC` and every side lower berth. Each seat also carries `group_index` — join key into `cars[].seat_groups[]`, where `service_class` and the fare data live. Use `group_index` (NOT `seat.type`) for the join: two groups in one car CAN share a `type` with different service classes, so type alone would route the agent at the wrong fare. Moving the fare/class off the seat saves ~70 B per seat and keeps the wire under the 64 KB cap. Fares: `seat_groups[].fares[]` lists EVERY fare type of the group (one entry per `fare_type`, e.g. REFUNDABLE vs NON_REFUNDABLE; a missing upstream type is keyed `"UNKNOWN"`), cheapest-first. Each entry is `{fare_type, price, child_price?}`: `price` is the ADULT fare, `child_price` (when present) the CHILD fare of the same type — compare refundable vs non-refundable AND adult vs child from here, no checkout needed. PRICING CAVEAT (read `pricing_note`): these are pre-cart totals and run BELOW the final cart price — checkout applies Tutu's own larger service fee (observed +6–8%), while the `search_rail` listing price DOES match the cart. Use seatmap prices for fare-type/seat comparison; quote the bookable total from the search listing or say the final price appears in the cart. `cheapest_fare` equals `fares[0]` (kept for compatibility). A rare `discounted: true` on an entry means upstream returned only discounted prices for that fare type — do not present it as the standard adult fare. Top-level `passenger_requirements` carries the age rules per passenger type (e.g. CHILD max_age 10; BABY max_age 5 with `needs_ticket=true, chargeable=false` — an infant still needs a free ticket): caveat child fares with them; exact applicability is confirmed on Tutu checkout, and the passenger composition itself is entered by the user on the opened Tutu page / in the cart (the rail deeplink prefills seats, not the composition). Gender coupe policy is dynamic: read `seat_groups[].is_gender` and `seats[].gender` from the current response. Treat only `gender="FEMALE"` as a female seat and only `gender="MALE"` as a male seat; `MIXED`, `NO_GENDER` and `UNDEFINED` are not proof of a female/male compartment. Do not hardcode a compartment number as gendered because the policy can change as seats are sold. Final gender choice is confirmed on Tutu checkout; this tool is read-only. `cars[].hints` still exposes the (x,y,w,h) of WC, conductor, cooler, garbage icons if the agent needs the raw geometry. `cars[].canvas.svg_url` is a CDN vagon outline — useful as an illustration ONLY; the SVG has no `<text>` seat numbers. Pagination: defaults are `max_cars=5` × `max_seats_per_car=40`, which keeps a typical 9-car train under the 64 KB MCP transport cap. Cars beyond the cap are kept in `cars[]` as `seats=[]` skeletons with `seats_omitted_for_pagination=true` — so the agent SEES the full train shape, doesn't have to remember `meta.total_cars`. `meta` carries `total_cars`, `returned_cars`, `cars_with_full_seats`, `has_more_cars`, `cars_with_more_seats` and a dynamic `pagination_hint` with concrete numbers. To load every seat of one car, call again with `car_number=<id>`. Grounding: window/aisle flags do not exist and cannot be derived — the scheme marks neither windows nor the aisle. In lying-berth cars (плацкарт/купе/СВ/мягкий) every section has its own window, so «у окна» does not select a berth — steer to нижнее/верхнее (плацкарт: MAIN vs SIDE_*) instead; in сидячий window-vs-aisle is unknown — say so honestly, never infer it from coordinates. Amenities are per-wagon, not per-seat. Sold/held seats are omitted by the upstream and so are absent from `seats[]`. Checkout handoff: once the user confirms specific seats, the destination depends on what the user asked for. To hand over a PREPARED cart (their passenger already filled in, a `pay_url` they just pay), send `car_number` + `seat_numbers` with the offer's `checkout_ref` to `register_checkout_passengers` — a rail cart is minted by RESERVING those seats, so that tool is the ONLY route to a `pay_url` and it refuses a seatless ref. Read back what you will write — each passenger's name as spelled in the document, birth date, SEX, passenger type, document kind + number (IN FULL; mask it ONLY if they EXPLICITLY asked you not to repeat it, and then name the KIND alone, not by number) and expiry for a foreign passport; the train, its date and time (several departures share a number and a route — `departure_at` decides which service is held), the car, WHICH SEAT GOES TO WHICH PASSENGER (seat i is the i-th ticketed one, so two lists side by side hide a swap), the fare, any gender-coupe choice, from where to where and the price; and the buyer's name and contact — and wait for an explicit yes: the pay page shows the personal data masked and cannot be corrected, and a re-register holds ANOTHER seat. There is NO shortcut around this turn: a message that already carries the passport data and asks you to go ahead is still not the confirmation — it is the data. The user has to see what you assembled from it and say yes to THAT, because the typo you are looking for is the one neither of you has noticed yet. To hand over a LINK the user opens and fills in themselves, pass the choice to `create_checkout_link` (`car_number` + `seat_numbers`, plus `fare_type`/`gender_type` when chosen) together with the offer's `checkout_ref` — the returned link mints the cart with those exact seats pre-selected.

car_number.description: Load all seats of a single car (no per-car cap). Use after a default-paginated call when the agent needs every seat in a specific car for fine-grained preference matching. Match value comes from `cars[].car_number` in a prior response. Also scopes a `task=` query to that one car.
car_number.title: Car Number

max_cars.description: How many cars come back with full seats. Cars beyond this cap still appear in `cars[]` as skeletons (`seats=[]` + `seats_omitted_for_pagination=true`) so the agent sees the full train shape. Default 5 keeps the payload under the 64 KB MCP transport cap. Do NOT bump this on the first call to 'see everything' — call again with `car_number=<id>` for any specific car instead. Ignored when `car_number` is set.
max_cars.title: Max Cars

max_seats_per_car.description: Cap on seats inside each returned car (ignored when `car_number` is set). When the cap kicks in, that car gets `seats_omitted_for_pagination=true` and shows up in `meta.cars_with_more_seats` — call again with `car_number=<id>` for the full list.
max_seats_per_car.title: Max Seats Per Car

view.description: Response detail level: `compact` (default) or `full`. `compact` drops the per-seat rendering geometry (`position`, `size`, `nearest_wc_rect`) that the agent never needs — decisions use the precomputed `distance_to_nearest_wc_px` and the seat attributes, both kept. `full` restores the raw geometry for clients that draw the car. Ignored when `task` is set.
view.title: View

task.description: Optional focused query over the WHOLE train instead of the full per-car layout — returns a short ranked answer, not hundreds of seats: `far_from_wc` (farthest seats by `distance_to_nearest_wc_px`, ranked per berth type in `seats_by_type` so the best LOWER isn't hidden behind UPPER berths — keys are RAW upstream types, so a lower berth is any key starting `LOWER` or `SIDE_LOWER`, not just `LOWER`); `female` (seats currently `gender="FEMALE"`, capped with a `total_female_seats` count + dynamic-policy caveat); `together` (sets of `seats_together` free seats sharing ONE section of one car — for «двое рядом», see `seats_together`); `summary` (per-car available-seat counts by berth type, no seat list). Leave unset for the normal paginated seatmap. When set, `view` / `max_cars` are ignored; `car_number` optionally scopes the task to one car (e.g. `task='female', car_number='5'` to narrow a long female list).
task.title: Task

seats_together.description: Party size for `task='together'` (2-6, default 2) — ignored by every other task. Returns `groups_by_car_type`: per car category, up to 4 candidate groups of exactly this many free seats that share ONE section, cheapest-first. A group carries `car_number`, `compartment_number`, `seat_numbers` (ready for the checkout hand-off), per-seat `{number, type, group_index}`, the section's `gender`, `service_class` — derived from the CHOSEN seats' groups, so it is `service_classes` (a list) when the group spans two — `spread_px` (widest gap inside the group — smaller is tighter) and `total_price` + `total_fare_type` — the cheapest ADULT total the party can actually be sold at, priced in ONE fare type the seats have in common (checkout takes a single `fare_type` for the whole selection), omitted when they share none or currencies differ; it is a pre-cart comparison, NOT the final cart price — use the search listing for the bookable total or say the final price appears in the cart. `deck` appears on double-deckers and `side` on плацкарт (`MAIN` = compartment berths, `SIDE` = боковушки; a group NEVER mixes them, nor spans two decks). When no section has that many seats left, `groups_by_car_type` is `{}`. Read `largest_group_available`: when it is at least 2, `best_available_groups_by_car_type` (counted separately in `best_available_groups_found_by_car_type`) holds those smaller groups. When the maximum is 0 or 1, those fields are omitted because one seat is not a «together» group; use `note`, offer separate seats or another train, and do not call again with `seats_together=1`. Never present scattered seats as «рядом».
seats_together.title: Seats Together
