tools.name: create_checkout_link
tools.title: Create a checkout link for a selected offer (Tutu.ru)
tools.description:
The single 'proceed to checkout' handle for a previously found offer. Call it as soon as the user commits to one option, however they word it — «беру», «самый быстрый из списка», «оформи», «забронируй», «дай ссылку» — and put the returned link in the same reply. It needs NO seat choice and NO passenger data in its default mode (the link opens the seat/room selection page). Pass the fields from the offer's `checkout_ref` object (emitted by every `search_hotels` / `search_avia` / `search_rail` / `search_bus` / `search_etrain` / `search_multitransport` result); the tool dispatches by `product_type` (or the `transport` alias). Returns `{checkout_url, kind, ...}`.

Every branch is a PURE URL builder — no network calls, no server-side cart, idempotent. The link is what the USER opens; their browser creates the cart in their own session. (We do NOT mint carts server-side: such a cart is session-bound and 404s for the user.)

The returned `checkout_url` is an OPAQUE string. Hand it to the user byte-for-byte as this tool returned it: never rebuild it from parts, re-encode it, drop or reorder query parameters, or swap in ids you saw elsewhere in the payload. The response deliberately carries SEVERAL id spaces side by side — e.g. bus `checkout_ref` holds both `departure_id` (the route id the link needs) and `departure_geo_city_id` (the dictionary city id, the same value as `meta.from.geo_id`) — and this tool already picked the right one per product. An edited link usually still loads, so 'it opens' does NOT prove it leads to the offer the user chose: the usual outcome is another offer or a bare search page.

Per product (inputs from `checkout_ref`):
- avia: returns BOTH `checkout_url` (a Tutu mtp-deeplink that 302-redirects to the ticket's purchase page — but ONLY if the user's browser already has a tutu session; a cold browser / Telegram in-app webview lands on the avia search for this route+date instead, where they pick the flight. Also falls back to search if the offer expired) and `search_results_url`. Present it as 'go book', not 'your cart is ready'. Inputs: `search_results_url`, `offer_hash`, `departure_geo_city_id`, `arrival_geo_city_id`, `departure_at`, `service_class`, plus `passengers_full` / `passengers_child` / `passengers_infant` (the searched party — forward them so the cart requests the SAME passengers; omit and the cart opens with one adult, so a multi-passenger total won't match — have the user confirm the count in the cart). Round-trip: also forward `is_round_trip` + `return_departure_at` from `checkout_ref` — a direct round-trip deeplink then carries BOTH legs in one cart. Connecting round-trips return `search_redirect`: `explicit/avia` currently supports one flight per direction. SEPARATE TICKETS (`is_multi_pnr` on a one-way offer): forward `checkout_ref.checkout_parts` too — this tool cannot put such a trip in ONE link, so it returns `kind="deeplink_parts"` with one purchase link per ticket in `checkout_parts[]` (`ticket`/`of`, `from`, `to`, `flights`, `checkout_url`) and leaves the top-level `checkout_url` on the SEARCH page. Give the user every link, in order, and say each is its own cart and its own payment. For a non-cheapest fare override `offer_hash` + `service_class` from the chosen `variants[i]` (keep forwarding `is_round_trip` + `return_departure_at`). For avia, while the user compares flights, show ONLY `search_results_url` and do NOT call `create_checkout_link` prematurely. Once they choose an exact flight and the tool returns `kind="deeplink"`, show `checkout_url` as the primary purchase link together with `search_results_url` as the fallback for browsing. When it returns `kind="search_redirect"`, show `search_results_url` as the search page and explain `fallback_note`; do not call it a purchase deeplink.
- rail: an `explicit/train` deeplink. TWO modes. (1) Seat page (default): inputs `departure_geo_point_id`, `arrival_geo_point_id`, `train_number`, `departure_at` (ISO) — the link opens the train's order page where the user picks seats. (2) Straight-to-cart (`kind="checkout_deeplink"`): additionally pass the seat choice — `car_number` + `seat_numbers` (from `get_rail_seatmap`: `cars[].car_number`, `seats[].number`; one seat per passenger) plus `offer_hash` + `segment_hash` from `checkout_ref` — and the link mints the cart with those exact seats pre-selected (works in a cold browser; the cart belongs to whoever OPENS the link). Optional: `fare_type` (the chosen `fares[].fare_type` from the seatmap, e.g. REFUNDABLE), `gender_type` (for gender-policy coupes: MALE/FEMALE — ask the user; omit for regular cars), and `search_id`/`result_id`/`card_id` metadata from `checkout_ref`. Use straight-to-cart ONLY after the user explicitly confirmed specific seats; the cart skips the seat wizard, so a silently wrong seat would go unnoticed. Falls back to the tutu.ru/poezda/order page (needs `departure_city_id`, `arrival_city_id`, `departure_station_code`, `arrival_station_code`) if the deeplink can't be built.
- bus: an `explicit/bus` deeplink. TWO modes, same idea. (1) Seat page (default): `offer_hash`, `departure_geo_city_id`, `arrival_geo_city_id`, `departure_at` (ISO). (2) Straight-to-cart: additionally `seat_numbers` (from `get_offer_details`'s `seat_selection.available_seat_ids`; one per passenger) + `search_id` + `departure_id`/`arrival_id` (all REQUIRED here — pass them through from `checkout_ref`). Falls back to the bus.tutu.ru/seats page (`departure_id`, `arrival_id`, `city_from`, `city_to`) otherwise.
- etrain: tutu.ru schedule page from `departure_etrain_id`, `arrival_etrain_id`, `departure_at`.
- hotels: an `explicit/hotel` deeplink. TWO modes, same idea as rail/bus. (1) Page (default, `kind="deeplink"`): `hotel_alias` + `check_in` + `check_out` + `adults` (+ `children_ages`, `search_id`) opens the hotel's page with dates/guests pre-filled for the user to pick a room. (2) Straight-to-cart (`kind="checkout_deeplink"`): also pass `offer_pack_hash` — a ROOM rate's `offerpack_hash` from `get_offer_details` (after the user picked a room) — and the link mints the cart for that pack, landing on the hotel page if the pack expired (fallback_to_details). NB the listing `best_offer.offerpack_hash` does NOT mint a cart — only a room-rate hash does. Page-mode fields ride in `checkout_ref`. Falls back to the pre-filled `fallback_url` page (`kind="hotel_page"`) if the ref has no `hotel_alias`.

`kind` ∈ `deeplink` / `checkout_deeplink` (rail/bus with seats; hotels with a pack) / `deeplink_parts` (avia separate tickets — links in `checkout_parts[]`, top-level `checkout_url` is the search page) / `search_redirect` (avia) / `order_url` / `seats_url` (rail/bus fallback) / `hotel_page` (hotels fallback).

product_type.description: Product type of the offer. `railway` and `rail` are accepted as synonyms. Optional when passing `transport` from checkout_ref.
product_type.title: Product Type

transport.description: Backward-compatible alias for `product_type`; matches the `transport` key emitted in checkout_ref.
transport.title: Transport

search_results_url.description: For `avia`: the avia.tutu.ru search-results URL emitted in `checkout_ref.search_results_url`. Always returned alongside the deeplink so the user can fall back to browsing the listing page.
search_results_url.title: Search Results Url

departure_geo_city_id.description: For `avia`: departure city id (`legs[0].segments[0].from.city_id`, also in `checkout_ref.departure_geo_city_id`). Required for the mtp-deeplink purchase URL.
departure_geo_city_id.title: Departure Geo City Id

arrival_geo_city_id.description: For `avia`: arrival city id (`legs[-1].segments[-1].to.city_id`, also in `checkout_ref.arrival_geo_city_id`). Required for the mtp-deeplink purchase URL.
arrival_geo_city_id.title: Arrival Geo City Id

service_class.description: For `avia`: cabin class of the chosen variant. Three input shapes accepted: Tutu's upstream code (`ECONOMIC`/`PREMIUM_ECONOMY`/`BUSINESS`/`FIRST` — preferred, lives on each variant as `variants[i].service_class` and on the cheapest in `checkout_ref.service_class`), IATA letter (`Y`/`S`/`C`/`F` — what `search_avia` was called with), or the raw deeplink integer (`1`=Economy, `2`=PremiumEconomy, `3`=Business, `4`=First). When overriding `offer_hash` for a non-cheapest fare family, also override this from the same variant — and keep passing `is_round_trip` from `checkout_ref` (a fare swap doesn't change the offer's round-trip-ness).
service_class.title: Service Class

passengers_full.description: For `avia`: number of adults the search was for (`checkout_ref.passengers_full`). Pass it so the deeplink requests the SAME party you quoted — omit and Tutu defaults the cart to one adult, so a multi-passenger total won't match. Forward `passengers_full/child/infant` from `checkout_ref` together.
passengers_full.title: Passengers Full

passengers_child.description: For `avia`: number of children (2–11 yrs) (`checkout_ref.passengers_child`). See `passengers_full`.
passengers_child.title: Passengers Child

passengers_infant.description: For `avia`: number of infants (<2 yrs, lap) (`checkout_ref.passengers_infant`). See `passengers_full`.
passengers_infant.title: Passengers Infant

departure_avia_id.description: Accepted from `checkout_ref` (avia orders-API city id, used by `register_checkout_passengers`); ignored here — safe to forward.
departure_avia_id.title: Departure Avia Id

arrival_avia_id.description: Accepted from `checkout_ref` (avia orders-API city id, used by `register_checkout_passengers`); ignored here — safe to forward.
arrival_avia_id.title: Arrival Avia Id

passengers_adult.description: Accepted from a bus `checkout_ref` (the adult share of the searched party, checked by `register_checkout_passengers`); ignored here — safe to forward.
passengers_adult.title: Passengers Adult

is_round_trip.description: For `avia`: pass `checkout_ref.is_round_trip`. A direct round-trip offer builds a TWO-leg deeplink (both legs in one cart) — the tool joins the per-leg hashes and adds the return departure from `return_departure_at`. Connecting round-trips return the search page because `explicit/avia` currently supports one flight per direction. Forward `return_departure_at` from `checkout_ref` alongside this flag; without it the tool falls back to the search page. Other transports ignore this field.
is_round_trip.title: Is Round Trip

return_departure_at.description: For round-trip `avia`: ISO-8601 departure of the RETURN leg's first segment (`checkout_ref.return_departure_at` = `legs[1].segments[0].departure_at`, e.g. `2026-07-19T10:00:00+03:00`). Required to build a two-leg direct round-trip deeplink; omit for one-way.
return_departure_at.title: Return Departure At

checkout_parts.description: For `avia` SEPARATE-TICKET offers (`is_multi_pnr`): forward `checkout_ref.checkout_parts` verbatim. It carries one entry per TICKET (`departure_geo_city_id`, `arrival_geo_city_id`, `departure_at`, plus `from`/`to`/`flights` labels) and the tool returns one purchase link per ticket (`kind="deeplink_parts"`). THIS tool cannot cover such an itinerary with one link — omit this and it can only hand back the search page. (That is this link hand-off's limit, not the trip's: where `register_checkout_passengers` is registered, the same `checkout_ref` fills ONE cart for the whole itinerary.) Present on multi-PNR offers only; other offers and other transports ignore it.
checkout_parts.title: Checkout Parts

offer_hash.description: For `avia`: the stringified JSON from `offer.variants[i].offer_hash`; the deeplink hashes are extracted from it to build the purchase URL. A direct round-trip offer_hash carries both legs — the tool joins them and needs `return_departure_at` too. For `bus`: the `offer_hash` string used as `trip[hash]` in the checkout URL. If your host auto-parses the JSON back into a dict, pass it as a dict — we'll normalise it.
offer_hash.title: Offer Hash

departure_station_code.description: For `rail`: origin station code (`dep_st`, e.g. `2000001`). For `etrain` this is retained as a compatibility/debug field.
departure_station_code.title: Departure Station Code

arrival_station_code.description: For `rail`: destination station code (`arr_st`). For `etrain` this is retained as a compatibility/debug field.
arrival_station_code.title: Arrival Station Code

departure_etrain_id.description: For `etrain`: origin station id for tutu.ru commuter schedule pages (`st1`).
departure_etrain_id.title: Departure Etrain Id

arrival_etrain_id.description: For `etrain`: destination station id for tutu.ru commuter schedule pages (`st2`).
arrival_etrain_id.title: Arrival Etrain Id

train_number.description: For `rail`: the Express-3 train number such as `022А`. Copy it from `offer.checkout_ref.train_number` — do NOT read `segments[].voyage_no`, which is the passenger display number and differs from the bookable number for through-trains (e.g. displays `060*Г`, books `059Г`).
train_number.title: Train Number

departure_id.description: For `bus`: origin route id for `search[from]` on bus.tutu.ru/seats. Prefer this field from checkout_ref.
departure_id.title: Departure Id

arrival_id.description: For `bus`: destination route id for `search[to]` on bus.tutu.ru/seats. Prefer this field from checkout_ref.
arrival_id.title: Arrival Id

departure_stop_id.description: For `bus`: display/debug origin stop geo-point id. Older checkout_ref objects used this as `search[from]`; new objects should also pass `departure_id`.
departure_stop_id.title: Departure Stop Id

arrival_stop_id.description: For `bus`: display/debug destination stop geo-point id. Older checkout_ref objects used this as `search[to]`; new objects should also pass `arrival_id`.
arrival_stop_id.title: Arrival Stop Id

departure_stop_name.description: For `bus`: display name for the origin stop. Accepted for pass-through compatibility; URL building uses `departure_id` when present.
departure_stop_name.title: Departure Stop Name

arrival_stop_name.description: For `bus`: display name for the destination stop. Accepted for pass-through compatibility; URL building uses `arrival_id` when present.
arrival_stop_name.title: Arrival Stop Name

passengers.description: For the bus fallback `seats_url`: number of passengers to prefill. Rail deeplinks/order URLs do not preselect passengers or seats.
passengers.title: Passengers

departure_geo_point_id.description: For `rail`: origin segment geo-point id (`checkout_ref.departure_geo_point_id` = `legs[0].segments[0].from.geo_point_id`). Required for the rail `explicit/train` deeplink.
departure_geo_point_id.title: Departure Geo Point Id

arrival_geo_point_id.description: For `rail`: destination segment geo-point id (`checkout_ref.arrival_geo_point_id`). Required for the rail `explicit/train` deeplink.
arrival_geo_point_id.title: Arrival Geo Point Id

segment_hash.description: For `rail` straight-to-cart: the offer's segment hash (`checkout_ref.segment_hash`). Required together with `offer_hash`, `car_number` and `seat_numbers` to mint the cart.
segment_hash.title: Segment Hash

car_number.description: For `rail` straight-to-cart: the chosen car (`cars[].car_number` from `get_rail_seatmap`).
car_number.title: Car Number

seat_numbers.description: Straight-to-cart seat choice, ONE seat per passenger. For `rail`: `seats[].number` values from `get_rail_seatmap` (all in the same `car_number`). For `bus`: ids from `get_offer_details` `seat_selection.available_seat_ids`. Pass ONLY seats the user explicitly confirmed — the link skips the seat wizard.
seat_numbers.title: Seat Numbers

fare_type.description: For `rail` straight-to-cart: the chosen fare type — pass the seatmap `fares[].fare_type` string (`REFUNDABLE`→1, `NON_REFUNDABLE`→2) or Tutu's integer code directly. ALWAYS pass it when the user picked a fare: omitted, the cart opens on the default (refundable) fare, which is pricier than a chosen non-refundable one. Unknown labels are omitted from the URL (tell the user to confirm the fare in the cart).
fare_type.title: Fare Type

gender_type.description: For `rail` straight-to-cart, gender-policy coupes only: which gender the compartment is sold as — `MALE`/`FEMALE` (ask the user; `MIXED`/`NO_GENDER` and ints 0..3 also accepted). Omit for regular cars.
gender_type.title: Gender Type

search_id.description: `checkout_ref.search_id` — the searchId of the search the offer came from. REQUIRED for the `bus` straight-to-cart mode; optional metadata for `rail`.
search_id.title: Search Id

seat_count.description: For `bus` straight-to-cart: number of passengers. Defaults to the number of `seat_numbers` passed.
seat_count.title: Seat Count

hotel_alias.description: For `hotels`: the hotel's `/h_<alias>/` slug (`checkout_ref.hotel_alias`, also `best_offer`/row `alias` from `search_hotels` or `hotel.alias` from `get_offer_details`). Required to build the `explicit/hotel` deeplink; without it the branch degrades to the pre-filled hotel page (`fallback_url`).
hotel_alias.title: Hotel Alias

offer_pack_hash.description: For `hotels` straight-to-cart: a ROOM rate's `rooms[].rates[].offerpack_hash` from `get_offer_details` — pass it once the user picked a specific room and the deeplink mints the cart for that pack (`checkout=true`), falling back to the hotel page if the pack expired (`fallback_to_details=true`). NB the listing `best_offer.offerpack_hash` does NOT mint a cart (the redirector falls back to the hotel page); only a room-rate hash from `get_offer_details` does. Omit to open the hotel page for the user to pick a room.
offer_pack_hash.title: Offer Pack Hash

hotel_geo_id.description: For `hotels`: the hotel's geo id (`checkout_ref.hotel_geo_id`). Display/debug; the page URL comes from `fallback_url`.
hotel_geo_id.title: Hotel Geo Id

fallback_url.description: For `hotels`: the pre-filled hotel page (`checkout_ref.fallback_url` / `best_offer.checkout_url`) — this is what hotels checkout returns.
fallback_url.title: Fallback Url

departure_at.description: ISO-8601 departure datetime from the offer's first segment (e.g. `2026-04-30T13:30:00+03:00`). Used by rail (`date`), etrain (`date`), and bus (`search[on]` + `trip[start_time]`).
departure_at.title: Departure At

tools.name: register_checkout_passengers
tools.title: Register passenger(s) on a cart and get the pay link (Tutu.ru)
tools.description:
NOT the default booking handle — that is `create_checkout_link` («забронируй» included): normally hand the link first, offer this tool as the opt-in next step, and reach for it only when the user explicitly agrees to hand over passport data — never open the exchange by asking for documents, and never register before the user has confirmed the summary of what will be written.
Register the passenger(s) the USER gave you (passport data) onto a Tutu checkout cart and return a `pay_url` — a hand-over link the user opens to PAY in their own browser session (it is a pay page, not a data-review page — read the data back first).
**For a FLIGHT this BOOKS: it places a real (unpaid) Tutu order before filling the cart** (trains, buses and hotels only mint a cart). It never CHARGES — the user pays on the linked page — but it is not a dry run: call it only after the user has confirmed THIS exact offer and given their passport data. The response carries the `order_number`.

**READ THE DATA BACK FIRST.** The pay page is a pay button over a MASKED summary — the personal data shows there as asterisks and nothing on it can be corrected — so your own reply before this call is the only place a typo can surface, and a wrong letter costs a NEW cart (on a flight, a SECOND unpaid order). So before calling, read back what you are about to register: every passenger's name in the document's own spelling, birth date, SEX, passenger type, document kind + number (+ expiry for a foreign passport) — SEX especially, because you usually infer it from the name rather than being told it, and a wrong one mis-registers the passenger on their ticket; the trip itself — FROM WHERE TO WHERE (the refs carry opaque geo ids, so the endpoints have to be said in words), the service, date, time, car/seats, class or room, price (on a train also which seat goes to which passenger, the fare and any gender-coupe choice; on a hotel the property and its city, the room and rate); and the buyer's name plus the email/phone the tickets go to (the buyer's own name is written to the cart too, even when they are not travelling). Then wait for the user to confirm it. Show the document number IN FULL — that is the default and it is not yours to soften: a typo in the number is exactly what this check is for, and the user typed it in this same conversation, so masking protects nothing and breaks the check. That turn is UNCONDITIONAL: a message that already carries the passport and says «оформи» supplies the DATA, not a confirmation of what you assembled from it — and the typo you are hunting is the one nobody has noticed yet. The one narrow exception is about DETAIL, not about skipping the turn: a user who EXPLICITLY asked you not to repeat their document gets it named by KIND, not by number, with everything else still read back. That request is the ONLY thing that hides the number — absent it, show it.

The `pay_url` is SINGLE USE and lives ~1 hour: the FIRST thing to open it gets the cart, everyone else gets a 404 (verified live). Never open or fetch it yourself to 'check' it — that spends it — and beware messenger link previews, which fetch URLs automatically. Hand it to the user as plain text, tell them it's theirs alone and good for about an hour. If it lapses or gets spent there is no cheap refresh: calling this tool again redoes the work (for a flight, a SECOND unpaid order), so ASK the user first.

Give the offer EXACTLY ONE way:
- `avia_offer` (the normal path for a flight): pass the search offer's `checkout_ref` fields — `offer_hash`, `departure_geo_city_id`, `arrival_geo_city_id`, `departure_at`, `service_class`, the `passengers_*` counts (they MUST match the passengers you send — they price the booking), plus `return_departure_at` for a round trip. We resolve it into the cart ourselves.
- `offer_pack_id` + `product_source="hotels"` (the normal path for a HOTEL): pass a ROOM rate's `offerpack_hash` from `get_offer_details`. The listing's `best_offer.offerpack_hash` is NOT one — it does not mint a cart.
- `offer_pack_id` + `product_source`: any other checkout-gw offerPackId you were GIVEN. An avia `search_*` offer id / variant uuid is NOT one (the cart API rejects those), so never derive it from a flight search — use `avia_offer` for that.
- `rail_offer` (the normal path for a TRAIN): the search offer's WHOLE `checkout_ref` plus the `car_number` / `seat_numbers` the user picked in `get_rail_seatmap` — one seat per TICKETED passenger (adult or child; an `INFANT` rides free without a seat), in the SAME ORDER as `passengers`. Reserving the seats needs the ref's `departure_station_code` / `arrival_station_code`, so don't trim the ref. Places NO order and charges nothing, but it DOES hold the chosen seat(s) with the carrier — so a repeat call holds ANOTHER seat; don't retry a train call without the user's OK.
  A TRAIN cart is minted by RESERVING those seats, so the seat is not optional paperwork: **there is no seatless rail cart and no `pay_url` without a seat**, here or on tutu.ru. No seats yet → call `get_rail_seatmap` and HELP the user choose — read the map and propose seats that fit what they asked for, then send the choice they confirm because the reservation holds real inventory — always, with no autonomous shortcut. Handing a LINK instead is never a downgrade: `create_checkout_link` takes the same seat choice and mints the cart from the link, with no passport data — prefer it whenever the user would rather fill the cart themselves. If `get_rail_seatmap` answers `seatmap_status="no_layout_for_carrier"` there is no layout to pick from, so the seats are chosen on Tutu: hand the user `create_checkout_link`'s seat page — the CORRECT outcome for such a train (a `checkout_url`, not a `pay_url`), not a defect to report.
- `bus_offer` (the normal path for a BUS): the search offer's `checkout_ref`. Places NO order. It carries NO seat choice, and the pay page is a payment summary rather than a seat picker — do not promise the user they will pick seats there; hand `create_checkout_link` (which takes `seat_numbers`) if the seat matters to them. The party must match what the offer was priced for: `checkout_ref.passengers` in total and, when the ref carries the split, `passengers_adult` / `passengers_child` per voyager_type — a child priced on a child fare can't be registered as an adult (or vice versa).
Each call mints a FRESH cart, so don't retry it casually.

`passengers`: one object per traveller — `first_name`, `last_name`, `middle_name?`, `birthday` (ISO-8601), `sex` (`MALE`/`FEMALE`), `document`, `voyager_type?` — `ADULT` (default), `CHILD` or `INFANT`; the party must match the offer's `passengers_*` counts. On a TRAIN a `CHILD` books the child fare and an `INFANT` rides free (no seat, ticket still issued) — quote child prices from `get_rail_seatmap` (`child_price`), and mind the age rules (`passenger_requirements`): each supplied `birthday` must fit the chosen CHILD/INFANT type on the departure date, or the call is refused before the cart is minted.
`document`: say WHAT the user gave you — `document_type` is a KIND: `RUSSIAN_PASSPORT` (внутренний паспорт РФ), `FOREIGN_PASSPORT` (загран), `BIRTH_CERTIFICATE`, `SIMPLE_DOCUMENT` (hotels) — plus `number` and `expires_at` (required for a foreign passport). We pick the exact type this cart wants; you do NOT need to know that a flight calls the same passport something else than a train does.
**Names must be in the document's own script**: a Russian internal passport on a TRAIN/BUS needs CYRILLIC names, while flights and foreign passports need the LATIN spelling AS PRINTED in the document. Ask the user for the right spelling — never transliterate it yourself (a name that doesn't match the document gets the passenger turned away). A mismatch fails before anything is written.
`customer`: the buyer's contact — `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `phone`. The tickets go to this email/phone, so read it back with the passengers.

Returns `{pay_url, pay_url_expires_at, cart_id, passengers_registered, validated, ...}` — a COUNT, not the registered data: the read-back above comes from the arguments you sent, which is what we write — we map the per-product document TYPE and canonicalise date FORMAT for the gateway (a bare `1990-01-01` becomes `1990-01-01T00:00:00Z`, same day), but never a name, a number, or the VALUE of a date. Hand `pay_url` to the user (it expires ~60 min after minting). Collect passport data ONLY with the user's clear consent; this tool sends it to Tutu to fill the cart. Keeping that data out of logs is a SEPARATE rule from showing it to its owner — the read-back is required, not a leak; just don't repeat it afterwards without a reason. Optional marketing/personal-data consents are NOT accepted on the user's behalf.

AviaOfferRef.description:
An avia SEARCH offer to book — the fields a search result's
`checkout_ref` already carries (same names as `create_checkout_link`).

Resolved into an `offerPackId` by the avia orders API, because no search
response carries one. Not PII: hashes, city ids, a date and the party
size.

offer_hash.description: The variant's raw `offerHash` from the search (`checkout_ref.offer_hash`). A dict is accepted because some MCP hosts auto-parse JSON strings.
offer_hash.title: Offer Hash

departure_geo_city_id.description: `checkout_ref.departure_geo_city_id` (the outbound city id). `departure_city_id` is accepted too.
departure_geo_city_id.title: Departure Geo City Id

AviaOfferRef.title: AviaOfferRef

BusOfferRef.description:
A bus SEARCH offer to book — the `checkout_ref` fields plus the party
size. Its offer pack already exists; `TutuBusPackClient` names it.

No seats here: the bus cart lets the user pick them on the paid page,
and `seat_count` only has to match the passengers.

passengers.description: `checkout_ref.passengers` — the party the offer was SEARCHED and priced for. Must match the passengers you send.
passengers.title: Passengers

passengers_adult.description: `checkout_ref.passengers_adult` — adults the offer was priced for. Forward it verbatim when present.
passengers_adult.title: Passengers Adult

passengers_child.description: `checkout_ref.passengers_child` — children the offer was priced for. Forward it verbatim when present.
passengers_child.title: Passengers Child

BusOfferRef.title: BusOfferRef

Customer.description:
The cart's contact / buyer. `time_zone` defaults to Moscow (every
PROD sample).
Customer.title: Customer

Passenger.description:
A passenger to register into a cart voyager slot.

`sex` is REQUIRED — there is no safe default (a silent male default would
mis-register every female passenger on their ticket), so the agent must
collect it (`MALE`/`FEMALE`). `voyager_type` accepts a label or a raw
integer code and defaults to adult (the slot rules constrain it). `age`
is accepted for compatibility but never forwarded — see
`to_voyager_payload`.

age.description: Accepted for compatibility and IGNORED — omit it. `birthday` is the single source of truth for age and is what reaches the cart; a number sent here is never forwarded, so it can neither help nor contradict the birth date the user confirmed.
age.title: Age

Passenger.title: Passenger

PassengerDocument.description:
An identity document for a passenger.

`document_type` is normally a KIND — what the user handed the agent:
`RUSSIAN_PASSPORT`, `FOREIGN_PASSPORT`, `BIRTH_CERTIFICATE`,
`SIMPLE_DOCUMENT`. The concrete gateway type is chosen per cart (a
Russian internal passport is `PASSPORT_RUS` on a train and
`PASSPORT_RUS_LATIN` on a flight), so the agent never has to know the
per-product spelling. A gateway type the cart named, or a raw integer,
is accepted too and passed through.

`expires_at` is required only for documents that expire (foreign
passport); omit it for an internal RU passport.
PassengerDocument.title: PassengerDocument

RailOfferRef.description:
A rail SEARCH offer + the seat the user picked — the fields
`create_checkout_link` already takes for `explicit/train`.

There is no rail "offer → offerPackId" endpoint for us to call: the cart
is minted by reserving the chosen seats via the seats-gateway, which
returns the `selectedOfferHash` `new_cart` builds the cart from (see
`tutu_rail_seat_choice`). Not PII: hashes, ids, a train number and a seat.

train_number.description: The Express-3 `route_number` from the offer's segment — NOT the display `voyage_no` (a through-train shows '060*Г' but books as '059Г').
train_number.title: Train Number

departure_station_code.description: `checkout_ref.departure_station_code` (Express-3). Required to register a TRAIN — forward the full checkout_ref.

passengers.description: Travellers to register (one per seat). READ THEM BACK to the user and wait for an explicit yes BEFORE this call — each name in the document's own spelling, birth date, SEX, passenger type, document kind + number (+ expiry). Include SEX: you usually infer it from the name instead of being told it, so it is the field most likely wrong. The pay page shows this data masked and cannot be corrected, so a typo costs a NEW cart (on a flight, a SECOND unpaid order). The turn is UNCONDITIONAL — a message that already carries these values supplies the DATA, not a confirmation of what you assembled from it. The one exception is about DETAIL: a user who EXPLICITLY asked you not to repeat their document gets it named by KIND, not by number. That request is the only thing that hides it — by default the number is shown IN FULL.
passengers.title: Passengers

customer.description: The buyer's contact (name, email, phone). All three are written to the cart — the buyer's name too, even when they are not travelling — and the tickets go to this email/phone. Read the buyer's name, email and phone back with the passengers and the trip, and wait for the user's yes before this call — unconditionally, as for `passengers`: a message that already carries these values is the data, not the confirmation.

avia_offer.description: The flight to book, from the search offer's `checkout_ref`. Resolving it PLACES an unpaid booking. Read this trip back to the user with the passengers before the call — what you are about to buy: from where to where, every flight with its date, time and cabin class, and the price. The user's yes to that summary is required, always. Provide exactly one offer source.

rail_offer.description: The train to book: the search offer's WHOLE `checkout_ref` plus the `car_number` / `seat_numbers` the user picked via `get_rail_seatmap` and CONFIRMED — one seat per TICKETED passenger (adult or child), in the SAME ORDER as `passengers` (seat i goes to the i-th ticketed passenger); an INFANT rides free without a seat. The seats are REQUIRED (the cart is minted by reserving them; without them use `create_checkout_link`'s seat page instead). Places NO order and charges nothing, but it DOES hold the chosen seat(s) with the carrier — a repeat call holds ANOTHER seat, so don't retry a train call without the user's OK. Read this trip back to the user with the passengers before the call — what you are about to buy: from where to where, the train, its date and time, the car, which seat goes to which passenger, the fare, any gender-coupe choice, and the price. The user's yes to that summary is required, always. Provide exactly one offer source.

bus_offer.description: The bus trip to book: the search offer's `checkout_ref` (`hash`, the city ids, `departure_at`). Books NOTHING and charges nothing. It carries NO seat choice, and the pay page is a payment summary rather than a seat picker — if the seat matters to the user, hand `create_checkout_link` (which takes `seat_numbers`) instead. Read this trip back to the user with the passengers before the call — what you are about to buy: WHICH BUS (the carrier and service — several operators run the same route minutes apart and this hash is what picks one), from where to where, the date and time, and the price. The user's yes to that summary is required, always. Provide exactly one offer source.

offer_pack_id.description: A checkout-gw offerPackId: for a HOTEL, a ROOM rate's `offerpack_hash` from `get_offer_details` (with product_source='hotels'). NOT an avia search offer id / variant uuid — the cart API rejects those; use avia_offer for a flight. Read this trip back to the user with the passengers before the call — what you are about to buy. This path takes ANY product's pack (see `product_source`), so read back whichever applies: the trip — from where to where, and WHICH offer on it, since the refs are opaque hashes: on a FLIGHT every leg of the itinerary with its date, time and cabin class (a confirmed economy is not a confirmed business, and an unchecked return or connection is still booked); on a TRAIN the train, its date and time, the CAR and WHICH SEAT GOES TO WHICH PASSENGER (the same seat number exists in several cars, and seat i is the i-th ticketed passenger — two lists side by side hide a swap), the fare and any gender-coupe choice; on a BUS the carrier and service, since several operators run the same route minutes apart; on a HOTEL the property and its city, the room and rate, and the check-in / check-out dates — plus the price. The user's yes to that summary is required, always. Provide exactly one offer source.
offer_pack_id.title: Offer Pack Id

product_source.description: Product of the offer pack (required with offer_pack_id): avia / rail / bus / hotels.
product_source.title: Product Source

tools.description: Read a `tutu://` server resource and return its content. Use this when your MCP client doesn't auto-surface server resources in the prompt. Valid URIs: `tutu://help/overview` (full agent guide — start here), `tutu://geo` (city/point ids), `tutu://status` (server + upstream health), `tutu://special-offers` (experimental inspiration only). Returns `{uri, mime_type, content}`.
